runConfig.positivePrompt: Static wide camera. One complete Ankylosaurus magniventris stands in the same low left-facing pose and visibly eats the fern directly in front of its beaked mouth. Make two clear bite-and-chew cycles: the beak opens a small natural amount, closes on fern tips, the lower jaw chews, and the head bobs down and up by a clearly visible but controlled distance. Several fern tips bend toward the mouth, release, and shake gently. Keep the broad armored skull and eye readable. Keep all four feet planted, the low broad torso and armor stable, and the complete tail with one integrated oval club completely still and fully visible. Preserve the exact attached identity, wetland background, lighting, crop, and fixed camera. Silent, calm, child-safe everyday feeding hypothesis for ages five to fourteen.
